::: {.lead}
This practice session is for your course project. You make five slides from
your report, check them with four checks, and rehearse a three-minute talk
with Presenter View. There are no new ideas: two short problems with the
lectures you had. Do each one alone. The results of the activities are at
the end of this worksheet.
:::

## Recall

- A slide has one idea and a few words; the details go in the speaker
  notes. Presenter View shows you the notes and a timer (Lecture 8).
- An AI outline can become slides (Online activity 9); every number and
  every claim is checked with your data (Lectures 9 and 10).
- An AI-use statement says where AI helped and how you checked it
  (Lecture 9).

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the whole report|a theme"}
Where do the details of a slide go?
:   in the speaker notes

What does Presenter View show you that the class does not see?
:   your notes, the next slide and a timer

An AI tool wrote the first outline. What does the last slide say?
:   where AI helped and how you checked it
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Five slides and four checks

Sami presents his canteen project: which items earn the most. His five
slides are the title, the question, the chart, the insights and the end.
To make them fast, he gives the five titles of his report the style
Heading 1 and uses **Home › New Slide › Slides from Outline**, or he asks an
AI tool for an outline of five slides. He pastes his chart from Excel on
slide 3. Then he checks every slide four times: **accuracy** (the numbers
are as in Excel), **claims** (the data shows each sentence), **pictures**
(they fit the topic and are fair) and **honesty** (the end says where AI
helped).

![Five slides for a three-minute talk.](images/five-slides.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="sims/deck-checker.html" poster="sims/deck-checker.png" title="Deck Checker: ready to present?" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Your five slides · 15 min"}
1. In **Deck Checker**, mark the problem of each of Sami's five slides.
2. Make `talk.pptx` with five slides from your report. Paste your chart
   from Excel on slide 3, and write two insights with numbers on slide 4.
3. Check your five slides with the four checks, and fix every problem.

*Your product:* the marks of Sami's slides and your file `talk.pptx`.

::: {.check}
Deck Checker: slide 1 is OK; slide 2, the picture does not fit (a big
restaurant, not a small canteen); slide 3, a wrong number (451 JD, but
Excel says 415 JD); slide 4, a claim that the data does not show
("Everyone loves sandwiches"); slide 5, no AI-use line. Your slides: every
number as in Excel, every sentence shown by your data, pictures that fit,
and an AI-use line on slide 5.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Four checks"}
Choose the check that fails.

::: {.match extra="the theme|the font"}
A slide says 451 JD, and Excel says 415 JD. Which check fails?
:   accuracy

A slide says "Everyone loves sandwiches." Which check fails?
:   claims

An AI tool wrote the outline, and no slide says so. Which check fails?
:   honesty
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Rehearse and present

A talk of three minutes gives each of the five slides about 30–40 seconds.
Sami writes short speaker notes, not a text to read. He rehearses once with
a timer in Presenter View before his turn. Then he looks at the class,
speaks slowly and ends with his main insight.

![Presenter View: your notes, the next slide and a timer.](images/presenter-view.png){width=100%}

{{< sim file="../week-10/sims/rehearsal-lab.html" poster="../week-10/sims/rehearsal-lab.png" title="Rehearsal Lab: Presenter View and the timer" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Rehearse and present · 15 min"}
1. Rehearse Sami's talk once in **Rehearsal Lab**, with each slide close to
   its plan.
2. Write short speaker notes for your five slides.
3. Rehearse your talk alone with a timer, and write the time. Present it
   when the teacher calls you.

*Your product:* speaker notes for five slides and the time of your
rehearsal.

::: {.check}
Rehearsal Lab: every slide says "about right", and the total is about 3:00
(the plan: 0:20, 0:45, 0:45, 0:45 and 0:25). Your talk: about three
minutes, 30–40 seconds for each slide. Too long? Cut one sentence on each
slide, not the chart or the numbers.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The talk"}
Choose the best thing to do.

::: {.match extra="present it anyway|speak very fast"}
The rehearsal takes 4 minutes, but the talk has 3. What do you do?
:   cut one sentence on each slide

The talk is at 2:40, and two slides are left. What do you do?
:   say the main insight and finish

You notice that you read every word from the slides. What do you do?
:   look at the class and use the notes
:::
:::

## Exercises

1. Name the five slides of a three-minute project talk.
2. Name the four checks for every slide.
3. A slide says 380 JD, and Excel says 308 JD. Which check fails, and what do you do?
4. About how long is each slide in a three-minute talk with five slides?
5. What do you see in Presenter View that the class does not see?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. The title, the question, the chart, the insights and the end.
2. Accuracy, claims, pictures and honesty.
3. Accuracy; write the number from Excel.
4. About 30–40 seconds.
5. Your notes, the next slide and a timer.
:::
